summary: Wyoming County steel tower erected in 1923 and staffed in 2017; DCNR listed it for replacement, and no source confirms whether that has happened.

facts.design: Steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab, entered through a trapdoor
facts.status_note: Scheduled for replacement in 2017; no source we read confirms whether the 1923 tower still stands.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (Pinchot State Forest)

events.note: 60-foot steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab erected
Scheduled for inspection before the fall fire season to see what repairs were needed
Charlie Womer's last fire season watching from the tower, per a March 2017 report
Scheduled for replacement; DCNR's program to replace 16 towers began in September 2017; a PA Environment Digest report on it lists Mehoopany among the targets

evidence.supports: Built 1923 as a 60-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 foot cab
evidence.quote: 1923: A 60-foot steel tower with a 7 x 7 foot cab erected.

evidence.supports: Tower located in Forkston Township, Wyoming County
evidence.quote: The tower Womer manned in Forkston Twp., Wyoming County, is also scheduled for replacement.

evidence.supports: Mehoopany scheduled for inspection in July 1946 ahead of the fall fire season, to see what repairs were needed
evidence.quote: Towers are being checked to determine what repairs, if any, are needed to bring them up to standard in preparation for the fall fire season.

evidence.supports: Mehoopany was on the list of towers scheduled for inspection, Lackawanna District
evidence.quote: Towers scheduled for inspection next week include: Mehoopany in Wyoming county.

evidence.supports: Charlie Womer watched from the tower for 13 years
evidence.quote: For 13 years, Charlie Womer climbed to the top of Mehoopany fire lookout tower in Wyoming County to watch over miles of countryside.

evidence.supports: Womer's last season was 2016 and the tower is scheduled to be replaced
evidence.quote: Last year was his last season watching for forest fires, and the tower is scheduled to be replaced.

evidence.supports: Tower staffed during the fire season
evidence.quote: All three towers are staffed during the fire season, which runs from around late March through early May.

evidence.supports: Current entrance is a trapdoor; new towers planned with a catwalk and regular door
evidence.quote: Instead of a trapdoor entrance, such as the one at the current Mehoopany site, towers will have a catwalk around the outside and a regular door between the catwalk and the cabin.

evidence.supports: DCNR began a $4.6 million project in September 2017 to replace 16 towers
evidence.quote: In September 2017, DCNR began a $4.6 million Department of General Services capital project to replace 16 forest fire lookout towers on state forestland.

evidence.supports: PA Environment Digest lists Mehoopany, in Pinchot State Forest, among the towers targeted for replacement
evidence.quote: Dry Land, Mehoopany and Bear Springs, Pinchot

sources.title: DCNR Initiative To Replace, Renovate Fire Towers Across The State

notes_for_editor: The 1923 build date and 60-foot height agree across the two newspaper-era and 2017 sources. The 2017 Times-Tribune article is the main current-use source; the AP version of it returned HTTP 403, so the Times-Tribune text was used. The PA Environment Digest copy in the cache is undated, so the September 2017 project start is taken from its own text. No source says whether the replacement was built or whether the 1923 tower was removed. A dated DCNR completion notice would settle it. Access and visiting rules are not described in any source.
